results.summary_before: This chip classifies an 8-bit input stream into a binary regime using a shift-only exponential moving average compared against a programmable threshold with hysteresis. It includes a persistence counter to require N consecutive qualifying samples before changing the output. The design is configurable via strobe pins for threshold, hysteresis, and persistence, and exposes the running average on outputs. It is tested with a cocotb testbench against a Python reference model and requires no external hardware.

results.summary_before: This design implements an 8-entry, 8-bit content-addressable memory (CAM) that supports exact matching, masked pattern matching, and priority-based resolution. It can be configured via control pins to write data, load masks, and search, returning the address of the highest-priority match within one clock cycle. The CAM is intended for compact pattern-matching and lookup tasks, such as network routing or data filtering. The project includes thorough documentation and is verified with Cocotb and gate-level tests.

results.summary_before: This design is a fully digital RGB LED driver that accepts WS2812 protocol data and controls three LEDs with 8-bit PWM per channel. It includes a dithering scheme for flicker-free dimming at low clock rates and can forward additional data to another driver. The design requires external LEDs connected to the outputs and a microcontroller to generate the slowed-down WS2812 input. It is notable for its robust clocked implementation and testbench.

results.summary_before: This design displays a static image of a plane flying into the sunset with a text overlay that types out character by character. It also includes demos for oscilloscope XY display PMODs, which can be selected via input pins. The design requires a Tiny VGA Pmod for the main demo and additional PMODs for the XY demos. The text animation may complete before the VGA monitor recognizes the signal, so viewing in a VGA playground is recommended.

results.summary_before: This design plays the Super Mario theme tune through a piezo speaker connected to the bidirectional pins in a differential PWM configuration. It requires an external piezo speaker or the Tiny Tapeout Audio Pmod. The design also copies the input pins to the output pins for testing purposes. It operates with a 100 kHz clock and is intended for audio output.
